column1: # Arabic (العربية, ar) interface catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:
#   context    usually empty. `preview` words sample text inside rendered previews (the Design
#              tab's style-set tiles), which must fit a small tile; it falls back to the plain entry.
#   source     the English text exactly as in the code (tl!(...), ribbon labels, command labels)
#   escapes    \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns, and a
#              trailing "…" in one needs one in the other.
#   Lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored. A missing entry shows in English.
# Clean room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label in ordinary
# Arabic computing vocabulary (Modern Standard Arabic, Microsoft Office Arabic terminology).
# No product localisation, string table or translated UI was consulted or copied; add entries
# the same way. Product, format and technology names (WordCraft, PDF, Markdown, MCP …) stay in
# Latin letters. العربية is right-to-left; the catalog's rows are parsed into visual order
# (i18n/bidi.rs) so the labels read right to left, while the shell keeps egui's layout.

column2: Craft AI runs a local Gemma model on this machine. Nothing you write here leaves it: no account, no cloud service, no telemetry — the panel talks to a model runtime on 127.0.0.1.

column2: A local model is not a frontier cloud model: it can be wrong, and a long answer takes its time on CPU. Check anything critical, and mind a model's size against this machine before downloading it.
